steps.observation: Work on this for 10 seconds; do not stop early. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here are the key differences between RNA (ribonucleic acid) and DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid):

1. Sugar Unit  
   • DNA contains deoxyribose (lacking one oxygen atom at the 2′ carbon).  
   • RNA contains ribose (with an –OH group at the 2′ carbon).

2. Nitrogenous Bases  
   • DNA uses Adenine (A), Cytosine (C), Guanine (G) and Thymine (T).  
   • RNA uses A, C, G and Uracil (U) instead of Thymine.

3. Strand Structure  
   • DNA is typically double-stranded, forming a stable double helix.  
   • RNA is usually single-stranded and can fold into varied shapes.

4. Function  
   • DNA stores and transmits genetic information across generations.  
   • RNA plays roles in decoding DNA into proteins (mRNA), in protein assembly (rRNA & tRNA), and in regulation (miRNA, siRNA).

5. Stability  
   • DNA is more chemically stable—ideal for long-term storage of genetic code.  
   • RNA is more prone to hydrolysis (due to its 2′-OH), making it shorter-lived and well suited for dynamic cellular roles.

6. Cellular Location  
   • In eukaryotes, DNA is confined to the nucleus (and mitochondria/chloroplasts).  
   • RNA is synthesized in the nucleus but functions throughout the cytoplasm (and also in organelles).

Together, these differences make DNA the main hereditary material and RNA its versatile partner in gene expression and regulation.
